![**How microbes can set a planet's temperature.** (*a*) Hydrogen feeds two groups and exchanges with an atmospheric reservoir. Methanogens make methane, which thickens an organic haze and cools the surface; acetogens divert hydrogen into acetate, of which a fraction f is recycled to methane. Temperature shifts the competitive advantage, and the climate responds over a time τ. Biomass export, omitted from the schematic, also reduces methane delivery. (*b*) Hydrogen requirement of each group against temperature, equation (2.3). The curves cross at T\* = 281.53 K; acetogens need less hydrogen below it and methanogens above it. The alternative dry-mass capacity ratio (grey dotted) moves the crossing to 297.15 K, just above the 297.01 K climate peak. The bar marks the published haze-cooling temperature range; capacity ratios are anchored at 30 °C. Kinks fall at the assay temperatures; shading marks the continuation below 277.15 K. (*c*) Steady surface temperature against hydrogen supply J for methanogens alone and for both groups, with fixed products, f = 0.5 and τ = 0. With both present, temperature holds at T\* across the coexistence range (shaded), the plateau of Seto & Akagi [@seto2007CoexistenceIntroducingRegulation]. At the reference supply (dotted) methanogens alone give 273.5 K. Inset: the haze response of Arney et al. [@arney2016PaleOrangeDot], case B, with the haze-cooling branch in bold and the two reference states marked. Dashed segments are the assumed low-methane bridge and high-methane plateau.](../../figures/fig1.pdf){#fig-1 width=100%}

![**Perfect control breaks down when the climate responds slowly.** Panels (*a*, *b*): reference state, fixed products, f = 0, after a 0.1% kick to acetogen biomass. The time axis is broken between 2,000 and 28,000 years. (*a*) Surface temperature at response times of 1 year (thin) and 10 years (thick). (*b*) Global cell counts for the same runs on a log scale; the dotted line marks one cell. At 10 years the acetogens fall below one cell at 1,830 years, where both traces stop. At 1 year both groups persist through 30,000 years, with late oscillations about 380 years apart; their amplitude is still changing. (*c*) Leading real part of the eigenvalues against τ for matched exact and graded states at f = 0.5 (habitat spread σ = 0.03 K, d = 10⁻⁴ yr⁻¹ for the graded state). Markers show the first loss of stability, at 1.10 and 38.5 years. The vertical axis is linear between ±10⁻⁴ yr⁻¹ and logarithmic beyond.](../../figures/fig2.pdf){#fig-2 width=100%}

![**Durability costs precision.** (*a*) Critical response time $\tau_c$ against local sensitivity |S|. Left strip: the 42 exact states (S = 0), 36 on the haze-cooling branch (filled) and six bridge states already unstable at τ = 0 (open, placed at the strip's base). Lines: the four dial branches, joining finite margins on one branch; ringed markers show where each crosses 30 years. Symbols without lines: the 122 graded states of the earlier grid, 42 uniform states with product feedback (grey, all at the ceiling) and 80 with resolved habitat spread (green; nine finite). Arrows mark lower bounds at the 10⁴-year search ceiling. The shaded band spans the four ringed 30-year crossings (bracket midpoints), 0.07–0.31 K per e-fold. (*b*) Steady temperature against hydrogen supply potential P for uniform habitats (σ = 0, black) and uniform habitat spreads of σ = 1, 3, 6 and 8 K (green, darker for wider), at f = 0.5 with fixed products and cell exchange d = 10⁻⁴ yr⁻¹. Shading marks the supply range in which a uniform community coexists (P = 0.229–0.457); the dotted line marks T\*. Open circles mark the last resolved state on each branch. The σ = 1 K curve passes through the last point of the d = 10⁻⁴ yr⁻¹ spread branch in (*a*), at P = 0.30.](../../figures/fig3.pdf){#fig-3 width=100%}

![**The mixture assembles where the losing group can persist.** (*a*) Global cell counts after a rare invader enters, in each direction, with fixed products, f = 0.5 and τ = 3 years. These are finite-census trajectories: a group below one cell is removed at the next ten-year census (20 and 10 years respectively). Crosses mark the first one-cell crossings at 18.3 and 7.4 years. (*b*) Surviving group in all 24 runs: every acetogen invasion ended with acetogens alone, and every methanogen invasion with methanogens alone. Diamonds mark the 8 of 12 settings where the reference mixture of both groups is locally stable. (*c*) Bulk temperature after an invasion in each direction (fixed products, f = 0.5, instantaneous temperature). With no refuge (grey), the run ends with the invader alone, at 294.4 or 273.5 K. With two small habitats held at 278 and 286 K (2% of the area each, cell exchange 10⁻⁶ yr⁻¹), both histories end at the same mixed state at T\* (dotted), 281.535 K; the two end markers coincide.](../../figures/fig4.pdf){#fig-4 width=100%}
